questions.q: According to the summary, which habit can quietly block you from happiness?
a: Placing too much emphasis on money
Spending too little time at work
Reading too many books
Having too much time to yourself
questions.why: Lesson 1 says money is necessary, but making it the focus keeps you from the fulfillment that comes from helping others.

questions.q: In the story about Joe, why does volunteering leave him happier than being paid?
a: Helping without expecting a reward brings more fulfillment
Paid work always takes more time than volunteering
Volunteering teaches practical skills much faster
Neighbors rarely pay what a job is really worth
questions.why: Lesson 1 contrasts Joe's empty feeling after paid work with the satisfaction of working hard for the school for free.

questions.q: What does the author say about spending time alone?
a: It nurtures the one relationship you can never leave
It is a sign that something is wrong with you
It should be avoided in favor of social plans
It only helps people who already live by themselves
questions.why: Lesson 2 argues that solitude builds your relationship with yourself and is the only time you can really get to know who you are.

questions.q: What did the author discover after spending a whole day by himself?
a: It became one of his most memorable and enjoyable days
He felt lonely and regretted leaving his phone
He realized he needed to socialize far more
He decided to repeat it only once a year
questions.why: Lesson 2 recounts a day alone with good food, a drive into the mountains and a favorite movie as a highlight of his life.

questions.q: What kind of friends does the summary say you should look for?
a: High-quality people who push you to be your best
Friends who share your current habits and comfort
People who rarely challenge your decisions
A large group you can call on for anything
questions.why: Lesson 3 warns against mediocre company and urges you to find people who will push you toward your full potential.
